properties.statement:
THE LOOP HAS NO NOTION OF A SESSION MID-BUGFIX WITH A USER WATCHING A BROKEN APP, AND UNDER THAT PRESSURE ITS CEREMONY IS SKIPPED AND ITS DASHBOARD IS NOISE. Alex's Grok 4.6 session, 2026-08-14, items 3 and 9 — filed as two, and they are ONE complaint seen from two sides.

CEREMONY (item 3). Tightening a three-line product rule cost: an epoch, two `record_change`, two typed merges, tests, two checksum accepts. 'The user was iterating a live bug. The loop is right for a first capture; it is slow for \"you implemented the wrong comparison.\"' ⭐ AND THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST IN THE WHOLE REPORT: 'AGENTS WILL SKIP SNAPSHOTS UNDER THAT PRESSURE — I ALMOST DID.' That is a discipline losing to urgency, reported by the agent who nearly lost it — the exact failure the served instructions already name ('a discipline that depends on being remembered loses to urgency every time; fire it on a trigger, not on virtue').

DASHBOARD (item 9). 'All session: ~62 never-asked gaps, 39 structural defects, 16 unproven claims, 10 unexamined artifacts. `next[0]` is ALWAYS detect-and-ask. The work was implement, user-correct, implement. That noise is worse when the user is waiting on a running app.' `loop_status` reports coherence debt truthfully and ranks it identically whatever the session is doing.

WHY THEY ARE ONE THING: both are the loop having exactly one posture. A first capture and a live bugfix are different phases of work, and reflow2 models neither — so the same ranking, the same ceremony and the same next-step advice are served to both. The report's items 3 and 9 are the cost paid at the write side and the read side of that single absence.

WHAT ALREADY BEARS ON IT AND IS NOT ENOUGH: `loop_status` takes a `contributor_id`, and `cap:scoped-analysis` scopes the detectors by region — but both scope by WHO or by WHERE, and this is a question of WHAT KIND OF WORK is happening. `dec:idea-scoping-exists-and-did-not-narrow-what-a-builder-sees` holds the open question, with a serious counter recorded against the obvious fix: `loop_status`'s contract forbids a scoped answer that could read as 'the design is clean', so any phase mode must RANK differently rather than HIDE.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a phase is something reflow2 should infer, or something a session declares — and if declared, whether an agent may declare it or only the user. Nobody has proposed a mechanism.
